summary: English and Urdu first-party discovery identified Punjab's PLRA/PULSE land-record and cadastral-map services. The current PULSE viewer exposed an ArcGIS Sargodha cadastral layer; its metadata and an exact WUP-point query returned one safe native OBJECTID-plus-polygon result. One sample is retained, while runtime readiness remains held.
queryAndRequestOutcomes: All executed discovery queries, URLs, viewer/configuration inspection, token-gated service checks, layer schema/CRS, exact-point query, and response limits are recorded in city-7487-bhalwal.json. No login, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, private credentials, TLS bypass, or unsafe-field request occurred.

custodians.name: Punjab Land Records Authority / Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhancement (PULSE)
custodians.scope: Punjab government land-record and cadastral-map services; PULSE exposes the Sargodha cadastral layer used for the Bhalwal point.

schemaAndCrs.parcelSchema: ArcGIS polygon Feature Layer, Sargodha layer 30
schemaAndCrs.geometryCrs: source WKID 102100/3857; retained GeoJSON is EPSG:4326

safeFieldAllowlist: stable native cadastral parcel identifier (OBJECTID OID)
scopeLimits: The exact WUP point and population are preserved in the city record.
The one exact-point hit is not evidence of citywide absence or complete Bhalwal coverage.
PULSE's own map disclaimer makes the cadastral lines indicative rather than a legal boundary determination.
Only canonical native ID and geometry are retained; no raw source attribute set is retained.
Packet completion is not source integration/admission.
uncertainty: Current public-token and service availability may change with the PULSE viewer.
The Sargodha layer's relationship to the exact urban settlement boundary was not independently qualified.
No independent serial reviewer has qualified a runtime adapter.
